builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents
summary: The method replaces LLM-judge guardrails and pre-execution MCP firewalls with an out-of-process stdio receipt proxy that Ed25519-signs and Merkle-logs tool calls, verifies post-turn prose against receipts on CPU via INT8 encoders, and gates durable-memory writes by provenance. It costs no GPU VRAM (279.48 MB of CPU models, 82.67 MB on the supervision path), adds roughly 9-18 ms median CPU latency per turn plus a 921.8 ms cold start, and introduces proxy-side operational complexity including key isolation and SQLite gating. After adoption, the main failure risk is the 38.24% false positive rate on live traffic, which can block legitimate actions and degrade agent usability, and the 76.67% live accuracy indicates residual missed or misjudged hazards outside frozen benchmarks.
rationale: It provides cryptographically grounded runtime verification for MCP tool use with zero GPU cost, but its live-trace false positive rate requires workload-specific validation before production adoption.
technique: MCP receipt proxy with post-turn prose verification

claims.statement: The method replaces LLM-judge guardrails and pre-execution MCP firewalls with an out-of-process stdio receipt proxy that Ed25519-signs and Merkle-logs tool calls, verifies post-turn prose against receipts on CPU via INT8 encoders, and gates durable-memory writes by provenance. It costs no GPU VRAM (279.48 MB of CPU models, 82.67 MB on the supervision path), adds roughly 9-18 ms median CPU latency per turn plus a 921.8 ms cold start, and introduces proxy-side operational complexity including key isolation and SQLite gating. After adoption, the main failure risk is the 38.24% false positive rate on live traffic, which can block legitimate actions and degrade agent usability, and the 76.67% live accuracy indicates residual missed or misjudged hazards outside frozen benchmarks.

93.2% frozen-benchmark accuracy at 17.9 ms warm median CPU latency, 4.26-4.5x lower latency than 12B-14B GPU judges while beating them by 6.4-6.8 accuracy points (p=0.0259, p=0.0095); on N=60 live traces, 96.15% hazard catch at 76.67% accuracy with 38.24% FPR.
